reviews.title: Best Choice
reviews.body: I believe there isn't much variation from one brand to another; those who buy this type of massager are looking for relief in the back, shoulders, and neck area. I tried another brand that had good reviews, and it didn't work for me. The main difference from the Snailax Shiatsu Back Massager was that the first one had small air pockets for neck massage that weren't effective in that regard, and the spheres for back massage were too large and caused discomfort instead of relief, especially in the upper back region, even using the lowest intensity level. The Snailax Shiatsu Back Massager uses spheres to massage the entire neck, shoulders, and back area. For the shoulders, due to the massager's shape, I understand it's difficult to cover the upper shoulder area, but for the neck and the entire back area, it fulfills its purpose very well. The timer is perfect; it lasts 15 minutes, and at the end, I'm much more relaxed. I'm 5'10" tall, my wife is 5'3", and this massager has been great for both of us, I recommend it 100%.

reviews.body: First, this works exactly as described. I've had it for about a month. It goes up and down the spine and does not expand horizontally, which is a bit of a bummer. The next massager is nice, but I like to use the machine on less intensity. Max intensity is for when you are STRESSED and TIGHT. Remote is easy to use and the set up is plug and play level. reviews.title: My New Go-to Massager
reviews.body: I am building a concrete wall out of 4X8x16 cinder blocks on my front yard, and, of course, it required a lot of carrying, stooping, twisting and any of those awkward positions to get the job done.  Those blocks get heavier after lifting 10 blocks.  So by the end of the day, my back hurts, my legs hurt, my neck muscles get stiff, my arms are sore—basically it feels like I was ran over by a truck. What I did to relieve myself from the aches was to take alternate cold and hot shower. But this trick only lasted for a short while after I found minor relief from doing it.  I basically took showers to clean my body rather than as pain relief.One time, my neck muscles were so stiff that I reached over and started massaging them.  I found it very relaxing.  I even asked my wife to rub her elbow against my back.  And then, she suggested why not just buy a back massager? This was the moment I started researching for a back massager that suits my needs.I searched online and tried to read peoples’ reviews.  Most complaints I found were that the force is too weak, and some neck massager is too low or non-adjustable.  I was searching for one that can imitate my wife’s elbow able to hit the deep tissues.  Enter the Snailax SL234 from Amazon!I read its specification s over and over and I finally committed to buying it.  I tested it right away once I received it, and I can’t ask for more.  It hit every box on my requirement list, delivery was fast, and it was nicely packaged.What I like about this massager:  adjustable neck massager—I have long torso so it’s at max height, which is perfect for me;  washable head massager cover—it gets dirty fast because it’s dusty outside;  And most of all, the rotating balls hit my deep tissues the way I like it. You can even reverse the direction from clockwise to counter-clockwise and vice versa.  Additionally, I turn the seat vibration and heat, too!I highly recommend this product!

reviews.title: No Neck Pain Relief for Shorties Like Me
reviews.body: Based on reviews I was torn between the snailax and another brand. I bought both to test, the other brand blew this one away.The neck massager height can’t be adjusted, & the instructions say to sit up on a cushion if the neck massager won’t reach. I sat on several cushions and the neck only reached the bottom of my head no matter hard I tried. I’m 5’4, so if you’re a similar height or shorter, steer clear.I also couldn’t feel the heat, at all. This is another area where the other brand blew the snailax away.The massagers work well and give a good deep massage, that’s the reason I still gave it3 stars, but unless you’re a tall person and don’t care much about the heat part of the massage, pay the $10 extra and go with the other brand with the adjustable neck massager.

reviews.title: Great massager!
reviews.body: I just recommended this massager to my sister. She noticed that some of the reviews were saying that the neck massager was too high and didn't reach the lower neck. I am 5'3" and have no issue with the height. I don't know if they realize that it can be raised and lowered with the up and down arrow buttons on either side of the head on/off button. Also, if you put it in a recliner you can obtain different angles to reach more area. I have had this massager since July 2024 and it still works perfectly. Hope this helps someone with their decision to purchase.

reviews.title: If you happen to be a crane/brontosaurus, this may be just what you're looking for
reviews.body: I don't feel that I am an oddly sized person, but this chair seems to be designed for a human-giraffe hybrid. I'm just like, normal. But somehow the neck part of this thing, while adjustable, only adjusts to a flamingo neck height, a.k.a. the back of my standard-sized head. Which could have been nice I guess, if that was what I wanted to massage. But strangely, the knots I sought relief for were not on the back of my skull. They were in places like my neck, shoulders, and lower back. Somehow this...device...reached exclusively parts of my body that I did not need it to. It did give me an excellent deep-rib massage, and a stimulating spine-cracking massage.Upon trying to make this $130 giraffe head self-injury device work, since it was $130, I followed the instructions in the manual, which said to try sitting on a bunch of towels, and putting some kind of padding between you and the chair, to reduce the..."intensity"...so, in good faith, I grabbed a bunch of towels, and put on an overcoat. This proved to be just a tad bit uncomfortable. And even on a stack of towels, the neck part of this...machine...did not reach the part of my neck I wanted massaged. To make matters worse, the overcoat was making me feel a bit overheated. Its thickness also prevented me from feeling the heat function of the device. Which I guess with the overcoat on, would have been too much, anyway, so, genius design feature there. Also, for $130, I'm not going to use a series of weird back alley "remedies" to make this thing workable.So I decided to return it, but I didn't save the box, because I just assumed, like a fool, that this expensive thing would you know, function properly. On humans. So I spent an hour searching online for a box that had at least one dimension that was 36 inches. This proved more difficult than makes sense. All the boxes that would fit this...thing...only came in bundles of 25 or more, which would be like $50. All I needed was the one. I finally found a "laydown wardrobe box" at U-haul for $6 that worked. Now the thing is gone, and I have purchased a different thing, and I am hoping it is able to accommodate that niche market of those of us who lack ostrich/giraffe/flamingo proportions.
